thread:
Maria K.: noticed a customer ticket — their Feb invoice is ~45M tokens but our usage dashboard shows 32M. they flagged an unexpected ~13M token delta. Can ops confirm?
Sanjay R.: thanks, pinging infra. did we have any eventstore or ingestion alerts around end of feb?
ingest-bot: detected write_latency spike on eventstore shard-7 2026-02-28T02:50:00Z -> 2026-02-28T05:10:00Z, queued events: 1.2M
Alex P.: looking at the ingestion logs — we have a 2h window where events were queued and batch-acked later. this could double-count if replay/backfill logic emitted duplicates to billing pipeline.
Julie T.: how do we reproduce the token aggregation? what's the canonical source for billed tokens, eventstore vs billing-aggregator?
Nina S.: canonical source for invoices = billing-ledger post-transform (ledger-service). dashboard reads near-real-time aggregates from meter-aggregator cache. reconciliation job compares ledger -> aggregator snapshots nightly.
Maria K.: ok. hypothesis: replay/backfill after the eventstore lag caused the aggregator to ingest same events twice, but ledger deduped later, or vice versa. need to trace token counts through the pipeline.
Sanjay R.: I can run a delta query across eventstream->aggregator->ledger for the window. running this command now:
```
# outputs per-hour token counts for window
python tools/compare_token_sources.py --start 2026-02-28T02:30:00Z --end 2026-02-28T06:00:00Z --sources eventstream,aggregator,ledger --output /tmp/delta.csv
```
Alex P.: also check replay tool logs for job ids around 1790xxxx. if a backfill job re-ingested events without idempotency keys it would inflate aggregator counts.
Julie T.: repo for replay: infra/tools/replay. config key is `--idempotent=true` by default, but we recently pushed a change that toggles it off for certain bulk runs. might be relevant.
Sanjay R.: partial results: eventstream tokens=31,980,412; aggregator tokens=45,172,101; ledger tokens=45,168,899 for that window. aggregator vs ledger close, eventstream much lower. looks like aggregator counted replays that originated outside eventstream?
Nina S.: ledger reflects what was billed. if ledger ~ aggregator then invoice number (~45M) matches billing pipeline. eventstream being lower suggests we missed some events upstream during the window — likely replay inserted missing events and those got counted by billing.
Maria K.: that fits customer complaint: their app emitted less than ledger shows according to their logs. we need to show chain-of-custody and confirm where duplicates or missing ingests occurred.
Alex P.: I found a replay job started at 2026-02-28T03:40Z job_id=rb-202602280340-77. config: `--source=eventstore-archive --target=aggregator --idempotent=false` 
Sanjay R.: ugh. idempotent=false. that can reapply tokens even if original eventstream later delivered the same message to aggregator. can we list the job output?
Alex P.: tail of job log:
```
[03:41:02] Fetch chunk 0: 120k events
[03:43:10] Push to aggregator: 120k events, tokens=2,111,432
[04:05:00] Resume chunk 5: 98k events
[04:07:20] Push to aggregator: 98k events, tokens=1,772,900
...
```
Julie T.: is there any unique message id preserved? replay didn't set original event ids when idempotent=false so aggregator created fresh ingestion ids. ledger later merged duplicates using original message hashes during billing transform?
Nina S.: billing transform has dedupe slide but only on ledger ingestion; if aggregator counts are used for dashboard, they will display pre-deduped numbers. invoices use ledger post-dedupe, but in our case ledger ~= aggregator which implies dedupe didn't trigger or replay produced non-colliding events.
Maria K.: action plan: 1) pause any active replays with idempotent=false; 2) run targeted backfill dedupe job against aggregator to collapse duplicates; 3) produce a reconciliation report for customer showing ledger vs aggregator vs their logs; 4) hotfix replay tool to default to idempotent=true and add CI check.
Sanjay R.: pausing now — aborted job rb-202602280340-77 (signal TERM).
Alex P.: starting dedupe pass now using tools/dedupe_aggregator.py --window 2026-02-28T02:30:00Z,2026-02-28T06:00:00Z --id_key message_hash. running in dry-run first.
Julie T.: I'll open a customer-facing thread draft with SRE wording: explain discrepancy, cause (non-idempotent replay), remediation steps, ETA for corrected invoice or credit.
Nina S.: ledger-team: please confirm whether we should issue a credit or adjust next invoice once dedupe completes. ledger-run id: lr-20260302-11 queued.
Maria K.: verification steps once dedupe completes: compare aggregated tokens post-dedupe -> ledger. run `python tools/compare_token_sources.py` again and attach CSVs. if delta < 100 tokens then we call it resolved.
Sanjay R.: dry-run dedupe shows potential reduction ~13,102,300 tokens in aggregator for window. switching to live dedupe now. job id: dedupe-20260302-09 started.
Alex P.: live dedupe completed. post-dedupe aggregator tokens=32,069,998; ledger tokens=45,168,899; but ledger unchanged — ledger still shows billed 45M. need ledger adjustment path.
Nina S.: ledger team confirms they can run an adjustment: create reversal entries for duplicates, run ledger reconciliation, and emit corrected invoice. ETA 24-48h for adjustment and audit trail.
Maria K.: thanks. Julie, please update customer with root cause + ETA and offer temporary credit. Ops: follow up with a postmortem and deploy replay tool fix (PR open: #512).
Julie T.: will draft message and route through legal. PR #512 changes default `--idempotent=true` and adds unit test.
Maria K.: recording action items: [Sanjay] close monitoring and verification, [Alex] ship replay fix, [Nina/Ledger] process adjustment, [Julie] customer comms. Marking incident as "metering: non-idempotent replay caused aggregator inflation".
Sanjay R.: adding a follow-up to run monthly reconciliation alerts to catch >5% delta between eventstream and aggregator within 24h.
Maria K.: thanks team — keep this thread updated with final invoice/credit details.
